replace.geometry_query:
Compute metric geometry from one policy-visible camera's published RGB-D and calibration: project world points to pixels, back-project pixels to world points, or summarise the valid depth of a rectangle.
Use when: a geometric quantity must be derived from calibration rather than estimated from the picture. The clearest case is world_points_m, which is the only way to ask where a world coordinate you already hold falls in an image -- for locating the commanded link6 target, a planned waypoint or a proposal's pregrasp point in the view you are looking at, and for reading whether it is in front of the camera and inside the frame. region answers "how deep is this patch" over a rectangle without naming a pixel. Near miss against mark_point: if you want a pixel measured, kept under a name and re-checked against a complementary view, call mark_point -- it verifies a repeated name across views, refuses a disagreement beyond 25 mm, reports depth-support counts and draws the overlay. This tool's points is the same back-projection without the mark, the name, the cross-view check or the image; prefer it when you want the number now and nothing retained, or when the pixel belongs to a saved step rather than the current observation.
Effect: read-only. It does not move the robot, change the scene, consume a robot decision, return any image, or persist a mark or reference; it reads the already-published observation artifacts and their calibration and returns numbers. Every result names the step and the source state it was computed from, and world_points_m additionally names the calibration hash it used.
Returns: exactly one of world_points, points or region_result, alongside step, source_state_sha256 and camera. world_points gives, per requested point, its camera-frame coordinates, in_front, in_frame, and -- when it is in front of the camera -- exact and rounded pixel_uv plus the scene depth already at that pixel and the residual between the two. points gives, per requested pixel, valid plus the median depth, the supporting sample count and world_xyz_m when depth was usable. region_result gives the rectangle, its valid sample count and fraction, and min/median/max depth when any sample was valid.
Does not: identify or segment an object, decide visibility or occlusion, or prove reachability, collision clearance, contact, retention or task success. A positive depth_residual_m means the scene surface at that pixel is nearer than your point, which is evidence of occlusion and not a verdict on it; in_frame is image bounds, not line of sight. A single-view depth reading measures a visible surface, never an object centre or its hidden extent, and no returned number is simulator ground truth.
On error: send exactly one of points, region or world_points_m -- none or two is refused and the message names all three. Use the named view's own top-left OpenCV pixel frame, keep every pixel and the whole rectangle inside that image, and order the rectangle [x0,y0,x1,y1] with x0<x1 and y0<y1. Missing or invalid depth fails explicitly rather than being inferred: move the pixel farther inside the intended surface, widen window_px, or read a complementary view. The camera list is fixed: head, left_wrist, right_wrist. The left_wrist and right_wrist cameras move with their arms, so their calibration is valid only at the pose they were captured at -- after any motion, query the fresh observation instead of reusing an earlier pixel from it. Adjacent calculation: use compute for arithmetic on already supplied world-frame numbers. Keep projection, back-projection and depth sampling here so they bind the selected observation and calibration.
replace.vision_ground: Retrieve up to three inspectable text-grounded target proposals from one selected current RGB-D camera. Use when: task language names an object or part and the scene-level search space should be reduced before the policy makes its own identity decision; begin with the widest useful view, then choose head or a useful wrist to resolve a concrete ambiguity. Treat the returned set as recall-oriented proposals: top rank and backend score are within-call ordering signals, not an oracle. Effect: read-only and creates one separate observation-bound target_ref per candidate. Returns: ranked candidates, source camera, bounding boxes, mask-area/depth summaries and numbered overlay; compare all plausible candidates against visible colour, shape, scale, location and surrounding context before selecting one. Does not: choose the correct candidate, guarantee that rank 0 is foreground, combine cameras, expose object ground truth, calibrate scores across calls, or prove absence when current coverage misses the target. On error: reject a candidate whose overlay or mask is dominated by table, robot, background or an implausibly large region even when its score is highest; inspect another returned proposal, rephrase a short visible description, switch current camera, or use vision_segment only after you can point safely inside the intended instance. Selection check: compare the requested task referent with every candidate crop and the original view; rank 0 and a high score do not authenticate identity. Separate an instance hypothesis from an observed property. Failed grasping is not evidence that the intended object is static or that a different object is the target. Revise a mistaken association when the visible evidence contradicts it. Boundary and mask/depth diagnostics describe observability, not semantic truth.
replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses. Select the arm on dual-arm embodiments.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the ARX X5 link6 controlled point; the embodiment card gives its fixed offset to the jaw contact centre. This backend supplies learned candidates only, with no geometry-derived top-down family. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. gripper_opening_m is the Panda-trained model's width prediction admitted up to the 80 mm nominal ceiling; aperture_calibration states that it is not measured pad clearance. Reachability is delegated to move_pose or grasp_execute; this call does not run a motion probe or return a plan_ref. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. After choosing a current candidate, use grasp_execute(candidate_id, rationale) when you accept its committed open/pregrasp/approach/close/lift/verify sequence without intermediate decisions. Choose manual move_pose plus set_gripper when you need a separate observation or decision before closing. Choose this path before moving: any world action stales the candidate, so call grasp_plan again before later using grasp_execute. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Put these fields under targets.<selected_arm>. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose and arm with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory. Prepared grasp selection: grasp_execute opens first and releases anything held, then uses the candidate pregrasp and contact poses and a 3 cm world-up probe. Select it only when opening and lifting are appropriate; otherwise use manual motion. Candidates are geometry proposals, not reachability certificates. For grasp_execute, the selected pregrasp receives one backend check before opening. Manual pose submissions use normal backend admission.
replace.place_plan:
Propose a bounded, numeric next placement step from selected current public RGB-D regions.
Use when: explicitly select the arm that holds or released this object; a retained object is near a visible destination and you need a preplace, lower, or short exit candidate. Select object_ref, then name the destination as flat fields: destination_kind, destination_support_ref, and destination_boundary_ref for open_container or front_cavity, which is refused by name when it is missing there and when it is supplied for support_surface. A whole-container centroid is not its cavity. Re-localize after every physical action.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world; creates an immutable observation-bound assessment, measured geometry and overlay. It consumes no robot decision, executes no motion and changes no action admission state. The original mask and depth are preserved as immutable evidence. In this placement-only projection, boundary discontinuity pixels are flagged uncertain, not certified background; the original depth remains available for inspection.
Returns: candidates, no_candidate or unknown with at most three one-step world-pose candidates, checks, stage evidence and hashed public evidence. For a current phase=lower candidate, use place_execute(candidate_id, rationale) when you accept the committed transport/descend/release/settle sequence. Set stop_before_commit=true if you need a fresh view before release; after status=stopped, use place_resume to continue or abandon. For preplace/exit candidates, or when you need separate decisions at other stages, use manual move_pose and set_gripper. After any world action, obtain current evidence and re-plan before selecting another candidate. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Put these fields under targets.<selected_arm>. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose and arm with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
assessment_ref is an audit reference, never an executable trajectory. Inspect the reported depth-edge uncertainty: all retained points still face unchanged support/opening tests. When boundary evidence is unresolved, candidates are conditional on unresolved silhouette, not full-object fit, passage or release certificates.
Does not: prove object identity, grasp attachment, stable support, physical release or official success; infer hidden cavity volume; or certify a collision-free scene/payload trajectory. The existing RoboDojo motion route is unchanged; this tool adds no scene or carried-object collision model. No visible conflict is not collision-free. upright uses a fit to the selected visible circular rim, not a PCA cup axis; absent/invalid rim evidence stays unknown. Each protected_before_refs and protected_current_refs entry at the same index is an Agent association, not identity authentication. A boundary depth gap cannot distinguish leaked background from a true farther surface or thin handle; flagged pixels remain unresolved evidence, not semantic background exclusions.
On error: inspect fresh complementary RGB-D and reselect functional regions; do not replace missing geometry with a guessed center or stale candidate. Retention checks supply advisory geometric evidence; decide closed-gripper motion from fresh observations and the reported uncertainty. For manual placement, inspect before release, release as a separate action, inspect after release and inspect again after a short departure. With place_execute, these steps belong to its committed stages; the optional pre-release stop is the available intermediate decision point. Use place_resume(abandon) before choosing a different placement. Each check is evidence for Agent judgment, not an automatic release or success authorization.
Arm binding: every gripper command, retention check and placement check must name the intended arm, whichever calls this surface advertises for them. Opposite-arm opening does not release this object; opposite-arm motion is not this arm's exit. All candidates stale after any world action, including motion of the other arm. A successful gripper receipt says executed, not Cartesian reached; it is command completion, not physical release. geometry_status and measured checks are separate from stage_evidence and uncertainty_reasons. Unconfirmed action stage preserves valid geometric candidates; inspect their prerequisites and decide subsequent actions independently.
replace.align_plan:
Answer, from inverse kinematics alone, which standoff poses facing one target from one named side an arm can actually hold.
Use when: you have a current target_ref and need an IK-only comparison of standoff poses from a named side. This is optional diagnosis, not a prerequisite for every approach. Near miss: this is not grasp_plan (where on this object do the fingers close); use grasp_plan for contact geometry and candidate finger poses; use move_pose when you already have the pose to command. An unreachable result describes this solver attempt, not an impossible approach side. If you later call grasp_plan, inspect its candidates independently: grasp_plan takes no approach_side or align candidate input, so it does not inherit this side selection. The five sides are world-frame directions toward the object and never toward an arm: top stands off above the target and travels down (world -Z), front stands off at -X travelling +X, back at +X travelling -X, left at +Y travelling -Y, and right at -Y travelling +Y. Choose the arm separately in arm; approach_side "left" does not mean the left arm. Two bounded numbers shape the request: standoff_m is the distance in metres from the target's visible-surface centroid to the candidate link6 position (default 0.10 m, permitted 0.02-0.30 m), and max_candidates is how many jaw rolls to sweep at that one position (default 3, at most 6).
Effect: read-only. No action is submitted, no world state changes, no artifact is written, and no observation is produced or consumed. Every candidate is solved by inverse kinematics from this arm's current measured joint configuration against its joint limits, so motion_planner_called is false in every result and the same request can answer differently after the arm has moved.
Returns: schema, the echoed target_ref, approach_side and requested_arm, motion_planner_called, and candidates. Each candidate carries source_index (which synthesised pose it came from, counting from 0), arm, align_pose = {position_m [x,y,z] in metres, orientation_xyzw [x,y,z,w] normalized} as a world-frame public link6 pose, reachable, position_error_m in metres and orientation_error_rad in radians at the best joint configuration the solver found, iterations (1 on this backend: one SDK IK solve per pose), rejection_reason (null when reachable; otherwise ik_failed when the SDK IK found no joint solution, ik_branch_jump when every valid solution needs a raw joint move larger than pi rad from the current configuration -- another arm branch the joint interpolation would sweep through -- or fk_residual_exceeded when a solution misses the pose by more than 0.01 m or 0.1 rad) and claim_boundary. All candidates share one standoff position and differ only by jaw roll about the approach axis. arm "both" returns one candidate per arm per pose, keyed by (arm, source_index). Unreachable candidates are returned rather than dropped, so a ruled-out side can be cited. Read position_error_m and orientation_error_rad rather than trusting the word reachable, then command a chosen align_pose through move_pose: under targets.<selected_arm>, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion and copy position_m and orientation_xyzw. Select interaction by physical intent. Schema example only; replace this illustrative pose and arm with your chosen current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
 There is no later receipt and no reference to resolve, because nothing was submitted.
Does not: prove that a collision-free path exists, plan or execute any motion, avoid the table, the other arm, the target or anything else in the scene, or promise that move_pose to a returned pose will arrive. A returned pose has not been tried: reachable means only that this model of this arm admits a joint configuration holding that pose. It is not a grasp, not a contact, not retention and not task success, and it makes no claim about the gripper, which is neither commanded nor read. The standoff is measured from the visible-surface centroid of the segmented mask, not from the object's true centre, so an occluded or one-sided view biases every candidate toward the camera. An unreachable verdict describes this arm from its present configuration; it is not proof that the approach is impossible. Use position_error_m and orientation_error_rad to interpret this attempt; do not turn them into a probability of path feasibility. Only the motion tool attempts the actual route. On this backend the two IK models measurably disagree: over 7,860 poses this tool synthesised from 500 measured target-and-arm states across 114 runs, it refused about 5% of the poses the backend's own 128-seed, collision-checked IK admits and called reachable about 4% of the poses that IK refuses. Disagreement is under 1.5% from top and right and 14-16% from back and front, and the backend admitted none of the left-side poses tried. None of those backend refusals was a joint limit.
On error: invalid_arguments naming standoff_m means the value left 0.02-0.30 m -- resubmit inside that range instead of retrying the same number. invalid_arguments naming approach_side means the string is not one of the five declared directions; re-read this tool's approach_side enum and select one of its values rather than inventing a synonym. invalid_arguments naming arm means the name is not an arm of this embodiment; this tool's arm enum is the complete list of what it has. target_ref_unavailable means no such segmented target exists and stale_observation means the reference predates the current observation: re-run vision_segment or vision_ground on the current view and use the new reference. target_geometry_unavailable is retryable and means the mask or its depth is too poor to locate a centroid, so obtain a clearer current view of that target first. ik_branch_jump is not a joint limit: the pose is holdable only from another arm configuration, so prefer another jaw roll or side, or move the arm with recover_pose or a free-space move_pose toward that side and ask again. When candidates are unreachable, use their residuals and current geometry to choose a different side, standoff or arm if that answers a specific uncertainty. Do not exhaustively sweep unchanged requests. A world move changes the starting configuration and invalidates target references; obtain a fresh target before another query.
replace.move_to:
Move selected public link6 controlled points to world-frame positions while holding each measured action-start orientation. Use when: the intended change is translation-only free-space repositioning and a position-only trajectory label is useful. Effect: world mutation; compiles through canonical move_pose with interaction=free_space, so the Runtime solves one SDK inverse-kinematics target and interpolates the joints within the command's reserved window of at most 20 native actions, stopping at measured arrival; the route is kinematic, not collision-checked. Returns: the later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to select a controller implementation; rotate, command a gripper, infer contact intent, avoid obstacles, or guarantee reachability. On error: inspect the named failure stage and current residual, then choose a reachable intermediate or recover_pose after a genuine motion failure. Numerical inputs: before using a newly calculated target component or angle, obtain it from compute. Copying a valid tool result, reusing unchanged-input results, holding a component or selecting a constant requires no extra call. Image/depth/calibration queries belong to geometry_query. Use the resulting values in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.move_pose:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public link6 controlled point to a stated position and orientation. Send one or both arms under targets; an omitted arm is not commanded. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in targets.<arm>. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name.
Effect: compiles the request once. It reserves up to 20 native actions of the task's native-action limit and stops at measured arrival. free_space always uses the global route: one SDK inverse-kinematics solve plus joint interpolation, a kinematic target that is not collision-checked, with no trajectory planner; precision uses one bounded local Cartesian step when the complete change is within 50 mm and 15 degrees and the global route otherwise; contact_approach up to 50 mm/15 degrees is local, while a larger contact approach first reaches a pre-contact pose on the global route and locally executes only the final 40 mm/9.3 degrees. Small in-place rotations may be local. Every stage uses measured convergence and a local failure never silently falls back to global.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose the global versus local route; avoid obstacles; change an exact requested orientation; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed local stage through another backend.
On error: an argument refusal names the field and the bound it violated, never a branch index. position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at targets.<arm>.translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. planner_failed means the bounded SDK inverse-kinematics solve admitted no joint target; plan_rejected means zero controller writes, including an inverse-kinematics branch jump (ik_branch_jump or local_ik_branch_jump) and workspace targets; not_reached means execution started but measured convergence or endpoint verification failed. Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs: before using a newly calculated target component or angle, obtain it from compute. Copying a valid tool result, reusing unchanged-input results, holding a component or selecting a constant requires no extra call. Image/depth/calibration queries belong to geometry_query. Use the resulting values in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.rotate_wrist:
Rotate the jaw line around the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating selected public link6 controlled points about each action-start local +X approach axis while holding link6 position, usually to align the jaw-closing line.
Effect: compiles to an exact pose. Rotations within 15 degrees use one bounded local Cartesian inverse-kinematics step; larger rotations use the global inverse-kinematics plus joint-interpolation route.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: expose a literal wrist joint, translate by request, infer object alignment, command a gripper, maintain contact force or change the signed requested angle.
On error: inspect the current link6 axes and residual; correct sign/magnitude or use move_pose when position must co-vary. A failed local rotation is not retried through global planning. Numerical inputs: before using a newly calculated target component or angle, obtain it from compute. Copying a valid tool result, reusing unchanged-input results, holding a component or selecting a constant requires no extra call. Image/depth/calibration queries belong to geometry_query. Use the resulting values in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.rotate_pitch:
Tilt the current approach axis while holding position.
Use when: rotating selected public link6 controlled points about each action-start local +Y jaw-separation axis while holding link6 position, usually to change the approach direction.
Effect: compiles to an exact pose. Rotations within 15 degrees use one bounded local Cartesian inverse-kinematics step; larger rotations use the global inverse-kinematics plus joint-interpolation route.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: expose a literal robot joint, imply that positive pitch is always world-down, translate by request, infer surface alignment, command a gripper or maintain contact force.
On error: inspect realized axes and residuals, then correct sign/magnitude or use move_pose when position must co-vary. A failed local rotation is not retried through global planning. Numerical inputs: before using a newly calculated target component or angle, obtain it from compute. Copying a valid tool result, reusing unchanged-input results, holding a component or selecting a constant requires no extra call. Image/depth/calibration queries belong to geometry_query. Use the resulting values in this tool's declared units and frame.
replace.recover_pose: Move selected arms to a named robot-only recovery configuration while preserving all gripper commands. Use when: a planner/execution failure or poor configuration makes ordinary waypoint correction inappropriate; choose previous to return to the joint configuration measured when that arm's most recent admitted pose action started, whether or not it arrived, and choose home for a deliberate return to the RoboDojo episode reset joints. Prefer one-arm recovery unless both arms genuinely require synchronized retreat. Effect: world mutation through the canonical recovery boundary; the stored joints are reached by joint interpolation with no planner or collision check, omitted arms receive no drive target, and a recovery does not replace the saved previous configuration. Returns: the later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival; available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. submitted public strategies and recovery mapping immediately; the next receipt and fresh observation report actual execution, residuals, preservation and drift. Does not: reset the episode, restore moved objects or evaluator state, release a gripper, reverse an old trajectory, undo physics, act as an emergency stop, model scene or payload collisions, or guarantee escape from contact. On error: inspect each arm result and scene state, retry one arm at a time or use the other strategy only when physically sensible; stop and finish with failure or abort if both recovery routes are exhausted or unsafe.
replace.check_task: Query the environment-owned official RoboDojo Boolean verdict at the current valid state boundary. Use when: fresh physical evidence suggests the requested arrangement may be complete, and always before finish_episode(outcome=success); a planner success, closed gripper or visually plausible placement is not a substitute. Effect: read-only call to the trusted RoboDojo checker and no world advance. Returns: task_success Boolean when available, or an explicit retryable unavailable result. Does not: explain the predicate, expose numerical tolerances, actor handles, target coordinates, task source or expert trajectory, change the world, or validate infrastructure quality. On error: wait for a valid state boundary and retry; never infer official success from action submission or visual appearance alone.

append.grasp_execute: On this backend a refused probe's summary also carries ik_candidate_counts (SDK IK solutions returned, valid endpoints, and those within the joint-jump limit), ik_outcome_counts such as no_valid_endpoint, and constraint_rejection_counts per filter; they describe one bounded SDK IK solve, not proof that the pregrasp is unreachable.
